item.title: Parents lash out at Sweden's 'absurd' teen deportations
item.description: This week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra features an interview with the father of a high school student facing expulsion from Sweden, as well as analysis of the latest developments on teen deportations.

item.title: 17th century wreck reappears from Stockholm deep
item.description: A 17th century Swedish Navy shipwreck buried underwater in central Stockholm for 400 years has suddenly become visible due to unusually low Baltic Sea levels.

item.title: INTERVIEW: 'Sweden is saying it wants experienced workers, but not their kids'
item.description: Software developer Besnik Barani works at one of Sweden's biggest engineering companies, while his daughter is a paid intern at Chalmers Institute of Technology. If the appeal in her teen deportation case fails, Sweden could end up losing both of them.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Sharp decline in immigrant unemployment, government earmarks 70 million for return migration, joint proposal to stop teen deportations rejected and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.

item.title: Sharp decline in unemployment for foreign nationals in Sweden
item.description: The number of people born abroad who are working has risen dramatically in recent years, and the gap between immigrants and Swedes has been shrinking since 2020, according to a new report by Nordea.

item.title: Swedish interest rate 'could be cut' in March
item.description: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, could cut the country's key interest rate as early as next month, a new report has predicted.

item.title: 'If I’d known, I wouldn't have come': How Sweden's teen deportations deter skilled workers
item.description: They study at some of Sweden's top universities and their parents hold senior positions at companies like Tetra Pak, Ericsson, and Volvo Cars. The Local has heard from more than 50 people affected by the teen deportation issue.

item.title: Everything you need to know about skiing on 'sportlov' in Sweden
item.description: 'Sportlov', the week in late winter which school children have off to do winter sports, falls somewhere between the start of February and the start of March, depending on the year and where you live. Here's what you need to know about getting to the slopes.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: sportlov
item.description: For most Swedish schoolchildren, February (or the beginning of March) is synonymous with sportlov, or the annual sports vacation. The vacation was initially created during World War Two as a response to Sweden's energy crisis.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Migration minister 'working on solution' for teen deportations, police unable to warn free schools if teachers are suspected and more news from Sweden on Thursday.
